court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Shaikh Naim S/O Shaikh Chand And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shaikh Naim S/O Shaikh Chand, others (husband, wife, children)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra and another (wife)

facts_of_case: Parties have arrived at an amicable settlement. Wife approached Family Court for maintenance. Parties agreed to dissolve marriage by mutual consent under Section 13(B) of Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Kulwinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2007) 4 CTC 769

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and the victim have settled their dispute, but before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.
legal_principles.held: However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime. Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Kulwinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2007) 4 CTC 769
keywords: nature and gravity of the crime

outcome.final_order: Parties' dispute settled amicably. Husband to pay wife Rs. 4 lakh as full and final settlement against streedhan and dowry maintenance in two installments.
